slots.title: Warsh’s first Jackson Hole speech at 10 a.m. ET
slots.body:
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s first Jackson Hole keynote is scheduled for 10 a.m.
ET today.

Coverage ahead of the speech describes U.S. stock futures as mixed and Treasury yields as little changed.

The 10-year Treasury yield was last marked at 4.7% on Aug. 26.

The gap between 2-year (4.2%) and 10-year yields was 0.47 percentage points on that same snapshot.

The CBOE Volatility Index finished the prior session at 14.5, down 0.1%.

slots.title: Trump raises bank-sanction talk as Xi visit prep continues
slots.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump said Thursday he could impose sanctions on Chinese banks, according to CNBC’s report on the U.S.–China relationship.

The same reporting notes that U.S. and Chinese officials are still moving ahead with plans for President Xi Jinping’s trip to the U.S. next month.

The headline frames sharper rhetoric from Washington alongside continued meeting preparation.

No new U.S. economic release in the injected calendar is tied to this story.

slots.title: French borrowing costs at 2008-crisis highs
slots.body:
French government borrowing costs have reached their highest level since the 2008 global financial crisis, per CNBC International’s report.

French stocks hit a one-month low in the same coverage.

The story ties the move to the first presidential debate before a key vote next year.

For U.S. readers, the piece sits alongside a day when global markets are also focused on the Fed’s Jackson Hole forum.

Germany exposure via the iShares MSCI Germany ETF ($EWG) closed up 0.6% at 44.58 in the prior session.

The FTSE 100 closed up 0.2% at 10,814.57.

slots.title: Shein lists in Hong Kong Sept. 1
slots.body:
Shein is set for a Hong Kong trading debut on Sept. 1.

Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing said it will allow short selling of Shein shares after listing, and will list weekly and monthly options and derivative warrants on the name.

That schedule marks when public two-way trading—and listed hedging tools—begin for the fast-fashion retailer’s Hong Kong shares.

Which part of the listing setup do you track first: the open, or the new derivatives?
